title: From Sparse to Dense: Visual Guide
outline: Title: From Sparse to Dense: Visual Guide

1. Words Versus Meaning | the query 'car mechanic' scored three ways - exact term overlap, a curated synonym rule, and dense vectors - with a slider over how rare the term 'car' is | a sparse scorer gives car and automobile different coordinates, so their overlap is exactly zero whatever idf weighting you choose, and dense retrieval fixes it by not using terms as coordinates at all

2. Kinds Of Mismatch | six query-to-document pairs (surface variation, synonym, abbreviation, symptom vs cause, ambiguity, exact identifier) each judged against analyzer, curated expansion, dense encoder and hybrid | vocabulary mismatch is six different problems with different fixes, and on exact identifiers and codes the dense encoder is the wrong answer - which is why you diagnose the query distribution before replacing anything

3. Truncating The Matrix | the term-document matrix for [car, automobile, engine, policy] over three documents, with a rank slider showing the singular values kept, the rank-k reconstruction, and the cosines it produces | SVD truncation manufactures soft matching by filling zeros in - at rank 2 the row for 'car' carries 0.104 in a document that never contained the word and car/automobile rise from 0 to 0.086 - while rank 1 merges every sense and full rank restores the original noise

4. Rotate The Query | the lesson's two-dimensional teaching model plotted live, with the query vector swung by a slider and the three documents rescored and reranked | dot products are projections, so the ranking is a property of the geometry rather than of the words - the paraphrase wins at 18.4 degrees, the exact-word distractor takes the top below -24 degrees, and the bicycle shop takes it past 68 degrees

5. One Vector Per Chunk | a 100-page manual split by a chunk-size slider from 40 words to the whole document, with vector count, focus and context, plus a toggle for carrying the section path into the encoded text | chunking decides what a document vector means, since one vector for the whole manual blends every subject while tiny chunks lose the context that made them interpretable and inflate the index
